sum: - Interested in Duke Energy Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

- Third-quarter adjusted earnings rose to $1.99 per share from $1.81 a year earlier. Duke narrowed its 2026 adjusted earnings outlook to $6.70–$6.80 per share and expects to finish near the top of the range.

- Electricity demand grew 2%, its strongest quarterly increase since 2022. Duke expects 3%–4% load growth over the rest of its five-year plan, with 5.2 gigawatts of data-center capacity on track to begin taking power in late 2027 and 2028.

- Duke's capital plan stands at $103 billion, with a potential $5 billion–$10 billion more for generation and transmission tied to large-load contracts. The company plans to add 16 gigawatts of generation capacity by 2031.

sum: Duke Energy reported stronger third-quarter results on Thursday, November 5, 2026, and raised the lower end of its full-year adjusted earnings outlook. Compared with the 118.35-euro quote in the latest own report from November 5, the current Lang & Schwarz quote is down 2.70 percent.
Duke Energy stock traded at 115.15 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 16:42:33 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026.

For the quarter ended September 30, Duke Energy reported adjusted and reported earnings per share of 1.99 US dollars, compared with 1.81 US dollars a year earlier. Revenue rose to 9.104 billion US dollars from 8.542 billion US dollars.

The utility narrowed its 2026 adjusted earnings-per-share guidance to 6.70 to 6.80 US dollars from 6.55 to 6.80 US dollars. Management said performance through the first three quarters positions the company near the upper end of the revised range and reaffirmed adjusted earnings-per-share growth of 5% to 7% through 2030.

Infrastructure investment recovery, higher sales volumes and favorable summer weather supported the quarter. Higher depreciation, interest expense, minority-interest effects and a higher effective tax rate partly offset the gains.

Electric Utilities and Infrastructure generated segment income of 1.817 billion US dollars, up from 1.658 billion US dollars a year earlier. Gas Utilities and Infrastructure reported a 19 million US dollar loss, an improvement from a 26 million US dollar loss.

Duke Energy is executing a generation expansion designed to add 16 gigawatts of capacity by 2031. The investment program supports demand growth but also leaves depreciation, financing costs and execution important for future earnings.

Duke Energy stock gains focus after Q3 earnings beat and guidance reset
sum: Duke Energy reported stronger third-quarter results on Thursday, November 5, 2026, and raised the lower end of its full-year adjusted earnings outlook. The utility said reported and adjusted earnings per share reached USD 1.99 for the quarter ended September 30, compared with USD 1.81 a year earlier, according to the company's Form 8-K release.
Duke Energy stock traded at EUR 116.75 on Lang & Schwarz at 14:18 CET on Thursday, November 5, 2026. Investors can follow the real-time quote of Duke Energy stock.

The company narrowed its 2026 adjusted earnings-per-share guidance to USD 6.70 to USD 6.80 from a previous range of USD 6.55 to USD 6.80. Management said strong performance through the first three quarters positioned Duke Energy to deliver near the upper end of the revised range. It also reaffirmed a long-term adjusted EPS growth target of 5% to 7% through 2030, based on the 2025 guidance midpoint of USD 6.30.

Management does not provide a long-term forecast for reported GAAP earnings per share. The company said the quarterly improvement reflected recovery of infrastructure investments in growing service territories and favorable weather. Higher depreciation on the expanding asset base, minority-interest effects, higher interest expense and a higher effective tax rate partly offset those gains.

Electric Utilities and Infrastructure generated segment income of USD 1.817 billion, up from USD 1.658 billion in the third quarter of 2025. The improvement included a USD 0.20 contribution per share from the segment, with rate-case impacts, customer volume and weather supporting the result. Gas Utilities and Infrastructure reported a USD 19 million loss, an improvement from a USD 26 million loss a year earlier.

Group revenue increased to USD 9.104 billion from USD 8.542 billion. Net income available to common shareholders was USD 1.551 billion, compared with USD 1.407 billion in the prior-year quarter. The reported effective tax rate rose to 15.3% from 10.8%, mainly because of lower amortization of excess deferred income taxes.
Duke Energy is executing a generation expansion aimed at adding 16 gigawatts of capacity by 2031.

CHCI's first multifamily acquisition in North Carolina will be the third acquisition in 2026 under the Company's Institutional Venture Platform, following The Reed and Woodland Pointe

Comstock Holding Companies, Inc. (Nasdaq: CHCI) ("Comstock" or the "Company"), a leading real estate company specializing in the development, acquisition, operation, and management of mixed-use, transit-oriented properties and data center developments, today announced that it has entered into a purchase agreement to acquire The Ascher, a 672-unit Class A multifamily property located in Uptown Charlotte, North Carolina (the "Purchase Agreement"). Upon closing, which is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, The Ascher will join Comstock's growing portfolio of premier residential communities.

Opened in 2016, The Ascher includes two 24-story residential towers offering studio, 1, 2, and 3-bedroom floor plans, approximately 13,000 square feet of ground-floor retail, and a controlled-access parking garage with more than 900 spaces. The two buildings share a 6th-floor rooftop courtyard that includes a regulation tennis and pickleball court, a bocce court, a putting green, covered lounge seating with cafe tables, fire pits, grilling area, fenced-in dog parks, and an on-site pet spa. Each tower also includes its own private rooftop pool and sky terrace with panoramic city views, fitness center, resident clubhouse and lounge, and grilling area. In-unit amenities include floor-to-ceiling windows, private balconies, well-equipped kitchens, and washers/dryers.

sum: Duke Energy has delivered a 3 year share price gain that is hard to ignore, yet the real question for investors is whether today's US$120.67 price lines up with the dividend stream that underpins the stock. With income still a central reason many people own utilities, the focus now turns to what that payout really justifies.
- The stock is up 53.3% over the past 3 years, which puts real pressure on the dividend case to explain why the equity has become this valuable.

- Duke Energy's recent agreement on data center costs with Amazon, Google, Meta, and Microsoft may support future capital spending and could influence how much cash is available for dividends over time.
- If you'd rather focus on earnings, this one's for you. See why Duke Energy's 18.2x P/E tells a different valuation story.
The issue now is whether the current share price is adequately supported by the dividend stream that the Dividend Discount Model (DDM) attributes to Duke Energy.
If you are weighing Duke Energy's valuation against its dividend stream and data center exposure, it can help to compare that lens across 42 power grid technology and infrastructure stocks

The Dividend Discount Model (DDM) looks at what Duke Energy's future dividend stream could be worth in today's terms. For this utility, the model leans on a current dividend per share of about $4.61, a reported return on equity of 9.21%, and a payout ratio a little above 71%. That combination yields an implied dividend growth rate near 2.7%, which is a relatively modest pace and broadly in line with a mature, capital intensive electricity provider.

Duke Energy stock: BTIG cuts Duke Energy stock target to USD 135
sum: Duke Energy stock (ISIN US26441C2044) was hit by a BTIG target cut from USD 141.00 to USD 135.00 on October 20, 2026, according to TipRanks. At Lang & Schwarz, the stock was trading at EUR 108.18 on October 21, 2026 at 4:41 p.m. CEST.

BTIG analyst Alex Kania retained a Buy rating while lowering the target to USD 135.00 from USD 141.00. The note previewed Duke Energy's third-quarter results and cited interest rates as a headwind on utility valuations, while also pointing to longer-term demand from large electricity loads, according to TipRanks.
A second October 20 note was more cautious. BofA lowered its target from USD 138.00 to USD 127.00 and kept a Neutral rating ahead of the quarterly report, as Markets Insider reported.

Duke Energy generated USD 7.59 billion of revenue in the second quarter of 2026, an increase of 1.10 percent from the year-earlier period. MarketBeat also reported adjusted earnings per share of USD 1.43 for the quarter, above the consensus estimate of USD 1.30, with revenue up 1.10 percent year over year.

As of October 21, 2026, Duke Energy had a market capitalization of USD 94.84 billion, a P/E ratio of 18.26 and a dividend yield of 3.57 percent. Its 52-week range was USD 112.40 to USD 134.49. The range places the stock below its yearly high while keeping the price above the low.

Duke Energy will publish third-quarter 2026 results at 7:00 a.m. ET on November 5, 2026, followed by an analyst conference call at 10:00 a.m. ET. The date was announced by Duke Energy on October 6, 2026.

The November report will test whether the 1.10 percent second-quarter revenue increase and the USD 1.43 adjusted earnings per share result can support the longer-term growth case cited by BTIG. The contrast between BTIG's USD 135.00 target and BofA's USD 127.00 target gives investors a clear measure of the disagreement over valuation.
